company_brief_text:
# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000-$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships (partner-led applied AI architecture) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s safety-centered identity makes enterprise implementation a commercial and trust-critical discipline. Partner-delivered work must make Claude useful in real operating environments while retaining strong expectations for
security, governance, quality, and responsible use.

The core scaling challenge is expanding delivery capacity through an ecosystem without allowing customer experience, technical rigor, or risk controls to vary materially by partner, geography, or use case.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that brings frontier-model capabilities to enterprise and developer audiences. Its public-benefit-company structure and stated focus on reliable, interpretable, and steerable systems create a
market posture in which responsible deployment is inseparable from product value.

Its commercial model combines enterprise software, developer platform access, and ecosystem-supported implementation. This is distinct from a services-first business: partners extend reach and implementation capacity, but Anthropic must
retain a coherent product, architecture, and trust standard.

The resulting operating model requires practical translation between research and platform teams, commercial organizations, customers, and third-party delivery organizations. Winning patterns need to be useful enough for field adoption yet
disciplined enough to remain supportable at scale.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic’s opportunity is to convert interest in generative AI into sustained, measurable organizational use. That requires more than technical access: customers need confidence that workflows, access models, user behavior, and operating
controls can mature together.

A recurring strategic tension is standardization versus customer specificity. Enterprises expect solutions suited to their data environments, industries, and change-management realities, while Anthropic needs reusable patterns that do not
create an unbounded custom-delivery burden.

The company must also balance speed with safeguards. Ecosystem participants can accelerate market coverage, but poorly designed implementations can create product friction, support load, uneven outcomes, and reputational exposure. Clear
architecture boundaries, escalation paths, and quality signals are therefore commercial infrastructure, not merely technical process.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
The relevant stakeholder environment spans revenue creation, technical product experience, adoption quality, and external delivery capacity.

- Partnerships stakeholders need an ecosystem that produces credible customer outcomes rather than nominal affiliations.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic serves business users, administrators, developers, and technical product teams through Claude offerings and developer-oriented platform access. That breadth creates different architectural questions across workflow design,
identity and access, integrations, evaluation, administration, enablement, and operational measurement.

Enterprise rollout guidance emphasizes a journey that includes environment preparation, organizational launch, learning programs, and expansion of usage. This indicates that implementation quality extends beyond a successful technical
demonstration. Strong solutions connect technology decisions with user adoption and measurable business outcomes.

Anthropic’s emphasis on reliability, interpretability, and steerability suggests that evaluation, observability, guardrails, and human operating practices should be considered early in solution design. The strongest ecosystem offerings
will make these concerns repeatable through documented patterns, not treat them as exceptional review items.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic presents a network of cloud, technology, and services partners focused on customer AI challenges. This points to an ecosystem model in which partners can influence discovery, procurement, integration, delivery, and long-term
customer value.

Services firms can multiply implementation capacity and industry credibility. Cloud providers can shape infrastructure alignment and route-to-market. Technology partners can extend Claude into adjacent applications and workflows. The
challenge is ensuring these distinct contributors operate from compatible technical and commercial assumptions.

A durable ecosystem motion depends on several connected mechanisms:

- Account collaboration that clarifies customer ownership, delivery roles, technical validation, and escalation expectations.
- Reusable solution patterns that convert broad AI demand into credible workflow and industry applications.
- Enablement systems that improve partner judgment, technical fluency, and implementation consistency.
- Quality measures that evaluate adoption and durability, not simply partner activity or pipeline volume.

The largest ecosystem risk is variability. Scale adds value only when customers receive a consistent level of technical credibility, operational readiness, and responsible deployment support regardless of delivery route.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic continues to position Claude for enterprise and developer use while providing material focused on organizational rollout and partner participation. These signals suggest that the market has moved beyond isolated experimentation
toward production adoption, broader user enablement, and repeatable deployment practices.

Research notes also describe reported investment in a Claude partner network and associated training infrastructure. If this expansion continues, the organizational need is to establish technical standards, partner segmentation, and field
operating rhythms before external capacity grows faster than internal coordination.

Enterprise buyers increasingly expect AI vendors to fit established cloud relationships, implementation partners, security requirements, and transformation programs. Anthropic therefore competes on the dependability of the full adoption
experience alongside the quality of its models.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Enterprise AI architecture that turns experimentation into governed, durable usage.
- Ecosystem technical leadership built on reusable methods, enablement systems, and quality standards.
- Cloud, services, and technology-partner experience that links commercial execution to delivery reliability.
- Leadership of customer-facing technical organizations in ambiguous, high-growth environments.
- Credibility with executive sponsors, technical practitioners, developers, administrators, and delivery leaders.
- Fluency in AI evaluation, governance, security, risk management, and operational controls.
- Field-to-product discipline that converts deployment evidence into prioritized improvements.
- Team-building experience for technical advisory organizations that must increase reach without reducing rigor.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Enterprise AI adoption requires organizational change and user enablement alongside sound technical implementation.
- Claude’s business, enterprise, and developer surfaces make cross-functional architecture judgment especially important.
- Anthropic’s safety-oriented identity makes responsible production use a meaningful commercial differentiator.
- Successful partner engagements can become reusable solution patterns, training assets, and product-learning inputs.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims must come from the governed resume and proof graph.

jd_context.content:
Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships
San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA

About Anthropic

Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic's products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities

    Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
    Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic's GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
    Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
    Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
    Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
    Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic's products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have

    7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
    3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
    Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
    Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
    Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
    Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
    A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have

    5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
    Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Compensation

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role's On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD

    Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.

# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000-$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships (partner-led applied AI architecture) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s safety-centered identity makes enterprise implementation a commercial and trust-critical discipline. Partner-delivered work must make Claude useful in real operating environments while retaining strong expectations for
security, governance, quality, and responsible use.

The core scaling challenge is expanding delivery capacity through an ecosystem without allowing customer experience, technical rigor, or risk controls to vary materially by partner, geography, or use case.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that brings frontier-model capabilities to enterprise and developer audiences. Its public-benefit-company structure and stated focus on reliable, interpretable, and steerable systems create a
market posture in which responsible deployment is inseparable from product value.

Its commercial model combines enterprise software, developer platform access, and ecosystem-supported implementation. This is distinct from a services-first business: partners extend reach and implementation capacity, but Anthropic must
retain a coherent product, architecture, and trust standard.

The resulting operating model requires practical translation between research and platform teams, commercial organizations, customers, and third-party delivery organizations. Winning patterns need to be useful enough for field adoption yet
disciplined enough to remain supportable at scale.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic’s opportunity is to convert interest in generative AI into sustained, measurable organizational use. That requires more than technical access: customers need confidence that workflows, access models, user behavior, and operating
controls can mature together.

A recurring strategic tension is standardization versus customer specificity. Enterprises expect solutions suited to their data environments, industries, and change-management realities, while Anthropic needs reusable patterns that do not
create an unbounded custom-delivery burden.

The company must also balance speed with safeguards. Ecosystem participants can accelerate market coverage, but poorly designed implementations can create product friction, support load, uneven outcomes, and reputational exposure. Clear
architecture boundaries, escalation paths, and quality signals are therefore commercial infrastructure, not merely technical process.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
The relevant stakeholder environment spans revenue creation, technical product experience, adoption quality, and external delivery capacity.

- Partnerships stakeholders need an ecosystem that produces credible customer outcomes rather than nominal affiliations.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic serves business users, administrators, developers, and technical product teams through Claude offerings and developer-oriented platform access. That breadth creates different architectural questions across workflow design,
identity and access, integrations, evaluation, administration, enablement, and operational measurement.

Enterprise rollout guidance emphasizes a journey that includes environment preparation, organizational launch, learning programs, and expansion of usage. This indicates that implementation quality extends beyond a successful technical
demonstration. Strong solutions connect technology decisions with user adoption and measurable business outcomes.

Anthropic’s emphasis on reliability, interpretability, and steerability suggests that evaluation, observability, guardrails, and human operating practices should be considered early in solution design. The strongest ecosystem offerings
will make these concerns repeatable through documented patterns, not treat them as exceptional review items.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic presents a network of cloud, technology, and services partners focused on customer AI challenges. This points to an ecosystem model in which partners can influence discovery, procurement, integration, delivery, and long-term
customer value.

Services firms can multiply implementation capacity and industry credibility. Cloud providers can shape infrastructure alignment and route-to-market. Technology partners can extend Claude into adjacent applications and workflows. The
challenge is ensuring these distinct contributors operate from compatible technical and commercial assumptions.

A durable ecosystem motion depends on several connected mechanisms:

- Account collaboration that clarifies customer ownership, delivery roles, technical validation, and escalation expectations.
- Reusable solution patterns that convert broad AI demand into credible workflow and industry applications.
- Enablement systems that improve partner judgment, technical fluency, and implementation consistency.
- Quality measures that evaluate adoption and durability, not simply partner activity or pipeline volume.

The largest ecosystem risk is variability. Scale adds value only when customers receive a consistent level of technical credibility, operational readiness, and responsible deployment support regardless of delivery route.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic continues to position Claude for enterprise and developer use while providing material focused on organizational rollout and partner participation. These signals suggest that the market has moved beyond isolated experimentation
toward production adoption, broader user enablement, and repeatable deployment practices.

Research notes also describe reported investment in a Claude partner network and associated training infrastructure. If this expansion continues, the organizational need is to establish technical standards, partner segmentation, and field
operating rhythms before external capacity grows faster than internal coordination.

Enterprise buyers increasingly expect AI vendors to fit established cloud relationships, implementation partners, security requirements, and transformation programs. Anthropic therefore competes on the dependability of the full adoption
experience alongside the quality of its models.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Enterprise AI architecture that turns experimentation into governed, durable usage.
- Ecosystem technical leadership built on reusable methods, enablement systems, and quality standards.
- Cloud, services, and technology-partner experience that links commercial execution to delivery reliability.
- Leadership of customer-facing technical organizations in ambiguous, high-growth environments.
- Credibility with executive sponsors, technical practitioners, developers, administrators, and delivery leaders.
- Fluency in AI evaluation, governance, security, risk management, and operational controls.
- Field-to-product discipline that converts deployment evidence into prioritized improvements.
- Team-building experience for technical advisory organizations that must increase reach without reducing rigor.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Enterprise AI adoption requires organizational change and user enablement alongside sound technical implementation.
- Claude’s business, enterprise, and developer surfaces make cross-functional architecture judgment especially important.
- Anthropic’s safety-oriented identity makes responsible production use a meaningful commercial differentiator.
- Successful partner engagements can become reusable solution patterns, training assets, and product-learning inputs.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims must come from the governed resume and proof graph.
